```{r}
### QAQC with Sonde data - ASHC temperture ###

ASHC_Temp_Sonde <- read.csv("Sonde_Data/output/Sonde Master Files/ASHC_Temperature_Sonde.csv")
ASHC_Temp_Sonde <- ASHC_Temp_Sonde %>% dplyr::rename(Date_Time = Date.Time, sonde_temp = value ) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(Date_Time = ymd_hms(Date_Time, tz = "UTC"),Date_Time_30min = floor_date(Date_Time, "30 minutes")
  ) %>%
  group_by(Date_Time_30min) %>%
  summarise(
    sonde_temp = mean(sonde_temp, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  select(Date_Time_30min, sonde_temp)
ASHC_Temp_Sonde


ASHC_Temp_HOBO <- read.csv("HOBO_data/output/HOBO_master_files/ASHC_Temperature_HOBO.csv")

ASHC_Temp_HOBO <- ASHC_Temp_HOBO %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Date_Time = lubridate::mdy_hm(Date_Time, tz = "UTC"), Date_Time_30min = floor_date(Date_Time, "30 minutes")
  ) %>%
  group_by(Date_Time_30min) %>%
  summarise(
    hobo_temp = mean(Temperature, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  select(Date_Time_30min, hobo_temp)


#merge data

#ASHC_temp_validation <- ASHC_Temp_Sonde %>% full_join( ASHC_HOBO, by = "Date_Time")
ASHC_temp_validation <- ASHC_Temp_Sonde %>%
  inner_join(
    ASHC_Temp_HOBO,
    by = "Date_Time_30min"
  ) %>%
  rename(
    Date_Time = Date_Time_30min
  )
View(ASHC_temp_validation)
 

ASHC_temp_validation <-na.omit(ASHC_temp_validation)

ggplot(ASHC_temp_validation, aes(x = sonde_temp, y = hobo_temp)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") + # Ideal 1:1 line
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "blue") + # Best-fit line
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Sonde vs HOBO Temperature",
       x = "Sonde Temp (°C)", y = "HOBO Temp (°C)")

# Fit linear model to check for systemic offset/gain
ASHC_cal_model <- lm(hobo_temp ~ sonde_temp, data = ASHC_temp_validation)
summary(ASHC_cal_model)

# Compute Error Metrics
#error_metrics <- ASHC_temp_validation %>%
#  dplyr::summarise(
#    Bias = mean(hobo_temp, sonde_temp),
#    MAE = mean(abs(hobo_temp - sonde_temp)),
#    RMSE = sqrt(mean((hobo_temp - sonde_temp)^2))
#  )

#print(error_metrics)


ashc_bland_altman_data <- ASHC_temp_validation %>%
  mutate(
    Average = (sonde_temp + hobo_temp) / 2,
    Difference = sonde_temp - hobo_temp
  )

mean_diff <- mean(ashc_bland_altman_data$Difference)
sd_diff <- sd(ashc_bland_altman_data$Difference)

ASHC_bland_alt<-ggplot(ashc_bland_altman_data, aes(x = Average, y = Difference)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean_diff, color = "blue", size = 1) + # Mean bias
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean_diff + 1.96 * sd_diff, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") + # Upper limit of agreement
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean_diff - 1.96 * sd_diff, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") + # Lower limit of agreement
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Ash Creek Bland-Altman Agreement Plot",
       y = "Sonde - HOBO", x = "Average Temperature")
ASHC_bland_alt
#lets save this graph so we can reference it again later

pdf(paste0(path = "HOBO_Data/output","/ASHC_bland_altman.pdf"), height = 6, width = 11)
print(ASHC_bland_alt)
dev.off()


#Values above 0 - the sonde recorded a higher temperature than HOBO
#Values below 0 - the HOBO recorded a higher temperature than the sonde
#95% of the differences should fall within the red dashed lines - "limits of agreement" 

#outliers can be due to : instrument malfunctions, timestamps not aligning perfectly, one logger out of water (most likely with the HOBO), fouling, or need for calibration

#For ash creek, it appears the sonde is reading on average 0.3-0.4C higher than the HOBO but there is variability in the data. There are periods of time when the sonde is reading +5 to -7C difference. the relatively wide limits of agreement and substantial scatter indicate that agreement between the sensors varied considerably among observations, with occasional differences of several degrees Celsius. The magnitude of disagreement also appears to vary across the temperature range, suggesting potential temperature-dependent variability in sensor agreement.


### CALIBRATION FOR CORRECITON FACTOR ###

ashc_calibration_model <- lm(
  sonde_temp ~ hobo_temp,
  data = bland_altman_data
)

summary(ashc_calibration_model)
coef(ashc_calibration_model)

ASHC_HOBO_corrected <- ASHC_Temp_HOBO %>%
  mutate(
    corrected_temp = predict(
      ashc_calibration_model,
      newdata = data.frame(hobo_temp = hobo_temp)
    )
  )

ASHC_HOBO_corrected

#we don't want to supplement it yet we want to test if it actually is predicitng new data
#this code is randomly splitting the paired data
set.seed(123)
n <- nrow(bland_altman_data)
train_index <- sample( 1:n,size = 0.70 * n)
calibration_data <- bland_altman_data[train_index, ]
validation_data <- bland_altman_data[-train_index, ]
#build the calibration model using only the training data
calibration_model <- lm(sonde_temp ~ hobo_temp,data = calibration_data)
summary(calibration_model)
#predict sonde temperature for the validation data
validation_data <- validation_data %>% mutate(predicted_sonde = predict(calibration_model,newdata = validation_data),error = predicted_sonde - sonde_temp)
#calulate the prediction error
RMSE <- sqrt(mean(validation_data$error^2, na.rm=TRUE)) #there are some large errors that are strongly affecting the RMSE value (0.9)
MAE<- mean(abs(validation_data$error), na.rm= TRUE)
RMSE
MAE

#The HOBO and Sonde temperatures have a strong linear relationship (R² = 0.981), with a calibration equation of #Sonde = 0.138 + 1.003 × HOBO. Independent validation indicated a mean absolute error of 0.51°C and RMSE of 0.89°C, #suggesting that corrected HOBO measurements can reasonably approximate Sonde measurements for data supplementation. #However, occasional large discrepancies were observed and should be investigated before applying the correction #across the entire dataset.
  #need to do HOBO data clean up before using to see if that helps the RMSE




#Lets combine the sonde and hobo data by supplementing any missing data from the sonde with the hobo data
combined_temperature <- ASHC_Temp_HOBO %>%
  left_join(
    ASHC_Temp_Sonde,
    by = "Date_Time_30min"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    temperature_final = if_else(
      !is.na(sonde_temp),
      sonde_temp,
      predict(
        ashc_calibration_model,
        newdata = data.frame(hobo_temp = hobo_temp)
      )
    )
  ) %>% mutate(
  temperature_source = case_when(
    !is.na(sonde_temp) ~ "Sonde",
    !is.na(hobo_temp) ~ "HOBO_corrected",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )#which data was source vs supplemented
)

View(combined_temperature)

#Lets see what the raw data looks like combined 
ASHC_Temperature_combined <- combined_temperature %>%
    mutate(Date_Time = as.POSIXct(Date_Time_30min)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(Date_Time, temperature_final)) + 
    geom_point() + 
    geom_line(size = 0.2, position = position_dodge(.4)) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(21, 22, 24, 25)) + 
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#CC79A7", "#D55E00", "#009E73", "#0072B2")) + 
    ggtitle("Ash Creek Combined Temperature Data") +
    labs(x = "Time", y = "Temperature (Celcius)") + 
    theme_classic() + 
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 20, angle = 45, hjust = 1), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20),axis.title = element_text(size = 20)) +
    scale_x_datetime(date_labels = "%b/%Y", 
                     date_breaks = "2 month", 
                     limits = as.POSIXct(c('2023-06-01', '2026-11-01'))) +geom_hline(yintercept = 20, color = "red", linetype = "solid", size = 1)
ASHC_Temperature_combined


```

```{r}
### QAQC with Sonde data - FENC temperture ###

FENC_Temp_Sonde <- read.csv("Sonde_Data/output/FENC_Temperature_Sonde.csv")
FENC_Temp_Sonde <- FENC_Temp_Sonde %>% dplyr::rename(Date_Time = Date.Time, sonde_temp = value )  

FENC_Temp_Sonde <- FENC_Temp_Sonde %>% 
  mutate(Date_Time = ymd_hms(Date_Time, tz = "UTC"), Date_Time = round_date(Date_Time, unit = "30 minutes")) 

FENC_Temp_Sonde


FENC_Temp_HOBO <- read.csv("HOBO_data/output/HOBO_master_files/FENC_Temperature_Sonde.csv")
FENC_Temp_HOBO <- FENC_Temp_HOBO %>%
  mutate(Date_Time = lubridate::mdy_hm(Date_Time, tz = "UTC"), Date_Time = round_date(Date_Time, unit = "30 minutes")) 
FENC_HOBO



FENC_temp_validation <- merge(FENC_Temp_Sonde, FENC_HOBO, by = "Date_Time", all = TRUE)
FENC_temp_validation 

FENC_temp_validation <-na.omit(FENC_temp_validation)

ggplot(FENC_temp_validation, aes(x = sonde_temp, y = Temperature)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") + # Ideal 1:1 line
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "blue") + # Best-fit line
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Sonde vs HOBO Temperature",
       x = "Sonde Temp (°C)", y = "HOBO Temp (°C)")

# Fit linear model to check for systemic offset/gain
FENC_cal_model <- lm(Temperature ~ sonde_temp, data = FENC_temp_validation)
summary(FENC_cal_model)

# Compute Error Metrics
error_metrics <- FENC_temp_validation %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Bias = mean(Temperature, sonde_temp),
    MAE = mean(abs(Temperature - sonde_temp)),
    RMSE = sqrt(mean((Temperature - sonde_temp)^2))
  )

print(error_metrics)


bland_altman_data <- FENC_temp_validation %>%
  mutate(
    Average = (sonde_temp + Temperature) / 2,
    Difference = sonde_temp - Temperature
  )

mean_diff <- mean(bland_altman_data$Difference)
sd_diff <- sd(bland_altman_data$Difference)

ggplot(bland_altman_data, aes(x = Average, y = Difference)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean_diff, color = "blue", size = 1) + # Mean bias
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean_diff + 1.96 * sd_diff, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") + # Upper limit of agreement
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean_diff - 1.96 * sd_diff, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") + # Lower limit of agreement
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Bland-Altman Agreement Plot",
       y = "Sonde - HOBO", x = "Average Temperature")


#Values above 0 - the sonde recorded a higher temperature than HOBO
#Values below 0 - the HOBO recorded a higher temperature than the sonde
#95% of the differences should fall within the red dashed lines - "limits of agreement" 

#outliers can be due to : instrument malfunctions, timestamps not aligning perfectly, one logger out of water (most likely with the HOBO), fouling, or need for calibration

# the graph is showing that the sonde and hobo have very little average bias and more measurements are agreeable however, it becomes more variable with higher temperatures - the HOBO may actually be exposed at low tide on occasion depending on tidal level. 
```
